Over the same three games, they conceded 145 points. These results leave the side with a point difference of minus 96 ahead of their upcoming fixtures.

Although the lawyer leading the case has reportedly been forced out, the decision ensures the legal challenge remains active. teams.heading: Scotland Women players visit grassroots clubs to inspire future talent
teams.body: Scotland Women stars have spent the week engaging with local clubs and schools as part of a Community Bus Tour ahead of the upcoming WXV series. Players including Evie Gallagher and Elis Martin held rugby sessions at Balfron High School and Lenzie RFC to connect with young supporters. Elis Martin noted, "Building a legacy is one of the most important reasons for why we do what we do," as the squad prepares for fixtures against Canada, New Zealand, and Australia.

teams.heading: Prop Stella Orrin eyes maiden Wales cap in upcoming WXV series
teams.body: Young prop Stella Orrin is targeting a senior Test debut this autumn as Wales prepare for the WXV Global Series. After earning her first matchday squad selection earlier this year, the 20-year-old remains optimistic about her prospects against South Africa, the USA, and Japan. While Orrin previously appeared off the bench during the victory over the Barbarians in June, she is now eager to secure her first official international cap, stating: "I really trust the coaches and the girls that are around me."

teams.heading: Argentina struggles at home as Australia secures 27-21 series advantage
teams.body: Los Pumas now face a challenging path following Saturday’s 27-21 defeat against Australia in San Salvador de Jujuy. Despite tries from Geronimo Prisciantelli, Joaquin Moro, and Boris Wenger, Argentina could not bridge the gap created by a clinical Australian side. The result leaves the team searching for answers, having managed only one victory in their last 5 home matches. Coach Les Kiss acknowledged the match was far from perfect, noting "clunky bits" in the visitors' performance that Argentina must exploit in the Mendoza return leg.

teams.heading: Les Kiss eyes smart changes after admitting to Argentina win clunkiness
teams.body: Les Kiss has promised tactical adjustments for the upcoming series finale in Mendoza after identifying “clunky bits” in Saturday’s 27-21 victory over Argentina. While Australia extended their winning streak to 4 matches, Kiss noted that his side struggled to manage the ruck and lacked compactness in defence against a high-pressure Pumas outfit. “We’re going to have to be better in that area next week,” Kiss said, though he praised his leaders for remaining calm while under pressure in the San Salvador de Jujuy altitude.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One reverses restrictive policy on naturalised player status
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has officially backtracked on controversial registration rules that would have categorised naturalised players as foreigners. Following legal challenges and a fierce backlash from players, the league confirmed that those who held Japanese citizenship by May 2025 will maintain their status as domestic players. Managing Executive Director Hajime Shoji admitted, "The criticism was much stronger than we expected. We underestimated the reaction," while promising that the league will better prioritise communication with affected athletes moving forward.

lead.why: The league's policy reversal on player eligibility is a significant institutional development affecting the national team's talent pool.

teams.heading: South Africa overcome All Blacks fightback to level the Test series
teams.body: The All Blacks saw their bid for a series-defining victory ended in Cape Town, as South Africa secured a 33-26 win to level the series at 1-1. Despite New Zealand scoring four tries to three—through Roigard, McKenzie, Carter and Savea—the world champions’ clinical edge proved decisive. Rassie Erasmus has since identified the All Blacks’ attacking ability in the wider channels as a primary concern, insisting that his side must better contain the visitors' one-on-one threats ahead of Saturday’s third Test.

lead.why: The series-levelling defeat in Cape Town is the primary news story affecting the All Blacks' current tour.
